chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from his brother Daram, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever is born in Islam is Arab, and whoever enters it willingly is superior to whoever enters it unwillingly. And the Mawla (client/freedman) is the one who is taken captive from his land and surrendered (to the Arabs), so that is the Mawla.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Mawla and the distinction between born Muslims and converts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to clarify the sociological status of early Muslims, distinguishing between those born into the faith (who retain the prestige of 'Arab' identity) and voluntary converts, who are deemed superior to those who entered under compulsion. The definition of 'Mawla' here specifically refers to a captive taken from their native land, reflecting the historical context of slavery and manumission in early Islamic society where origin and mode of entry influenced social hierarchy.
